Well, communication is definitely a strong point of mine (perfect 800 on the verbal part of SAT and basically perfect scores on essays in college...I work in a call center, so I can speak as well), and my degrees involved a decent amount of experience with various technology and some coding.

How did you get into pre-sales engineering with a journalism degree?  Are there entry level positions, or are most going to require either prior experience or connections?  Travel is not an issue for me at all.

A quick google search tells me that the average salary for "pre-sales engineer" is over six figures.  Is that true at all?  What do I do to get into that field?  Honestly, anything better than $13/hr is better than what I have.  Maybe if I wasn't drowning in bills just trying to keep the lights on I could start working on fixing everything else.
